proofUses.reason: The last pivotal bridge leaves two terminal paths meeting the marked set. Attaching the extra connection to their union gives the two intermediate cases, including empty segments and coincident vertices.

BK is applied within each independent configuration after the path decomposition. A transition on pairs has mass at most twice the product of the two triangle quantities; no division by a connection probability is needed.
Cosine splitting and an explicit change of variables give the unrefined first-order estimate. The sharper (7.2.15) and higher-order (7.5.4) are not claimed.

Finite critical clusters stabilize under the uniform coupling. Critical witness diagrams dominate each fixed-order sum; a uniform geometric tail then gives convergence in the summable norm without asserting monotonicity of the cutting events.

The first-step bound replaces a possibly signed Fourier factor by a spatial bound with squared step factors. A bounded infrared constant and bounded critical edge mass imply a weighted triangle of order inverse dimension. The bootstrap premises remain explicit.
